chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Jabir Al-Makouf, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Be cautious regarding your religion, so veil it with dissimulation (Taqiyya), for there is no faith for the one who has no dissimulation for himself. Indeed, you are among the people like bees are among birds. If the birds knew what is in the interiors of the bees, nothing would remain of them except that they would eat it. And if the people knew what is in your interiors, that you love us, the People of the Household, they would eat you with their tongues, and destroy you in private and in public. May Allah have mercy on a servant from you who was upon our Wilayah.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation or veiling of faith/feelings for protection

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyya in Shia theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes Taqiyya as a fundamental pillar of faith, asserting that 'there is no faith without dissimulation,' thereby elevating it from mere precaution to a spiritual necessity. The metaphor of bees and birds illustrates the vulnerability of the Shia's hidden spiritual essence (Wilayah) to external consumption, emphasizing the need for concealment to preserve religious identity. This hadith underscores the historical reality of minority status and the strategic wisdom of maintaining inner conviction while navigating external hostility.
